concept.name: Lower high
concept.definition: A swing high that forms below the previous swing high. Together with lower lows, a sequence of lower highs constitutes the structural definition of a downtrend and shows weakening buying pressure on rallies.
concept.intuition: Each bounce runs out of energy sooner than the last — the ceiling keeps sinking.
concept.mechanics: Identified by comparing successive reaction peaks: when the latest rally high stalls below the prior peak, a lower high is printed. A break above the most recent lower high is conventionally treated as a warning that the downtrend structure may be changing.
concept.failure_modes: Lower highs are frequently exceeded in bear-market rallies, which can retrace large portions of a decline before the downtrend resumes.
concept.misconceptions: That a lower high guarantees further declines; it is one observation in a sequence and says nothing certain about the next move.
concept.example: A stock in a downtrend bounces to 95 after previously peaking at 100, then rolls over: the lower high at 95 confirms sellers remain in control.
